source_version: Capella (continuously deployed, no discrete version number)

concepts.label: curl() function
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the JavaScript language construct Eventing Functions use to call external REST APIs over HTTP/HTTPS

concepts.label: URL binding
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - the 'URL' binding type named in add-eventing-functions.json's binding table; this page is where its authentication/cookie/encryption behavior is specified in full

concepts.label: CurlError
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the JavaScript exception type (inheriting from Error) thrown by curl() on unexpected failure

relations.subject: eventing:curl-function
relations.evidence: To access an HTTP server using cURL, the Eventing Function needs to declare a URL binding and pass the alias of the binding to curl() calls.

relations.subject: eventing:curl-function
relations.evidence: The binding specifies the remote URL to be accessed and all calls made using such a binding are limited to descendants of the URL specified in the binding.

relations.subject: eventing:url-binding
relations.evidence: The binding may also specify the authentication mechanism and credentials to use. Basic, Digest and Bearer authentication methods are supported.

relations.subject: eventing:curl-function
relations.evidence: method - The HTTP method of the cURL request. Must be a string having one of the following values: GET | POST | PUT | HEAD | DELETE.

relations.subject: eventing:curl-function
relations.evidence:
encoding - Optional. A directive on how to encode the body. A string having one of following values:  
FORM | JSON | TEXT | BINARY.

relations.subject: eventing:curl-function
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - verb phrase for a documented exception-on-failure contract; no existing predicate covers exception behavior
relations.evidence: Exceptions Thrown - When an unexpected error occurs, a JavaScript exception of type CurlError inheriting from the JavaScript Error class will be thrown.

relations.subject: eventing:url-binding
relations.evidence: Note that Eventing utilizes multiple workers and multiple HTTP cURL sessions and so a Eventing Function cannot rely on all requests executing on the same HTTP session.

notable_absence.finding: The page states 'The target of a URL binding should not be a node that belongs to the Couchbase cluster' but does not explain what happens if it is - no error behavior, validation step, or enforcement mechanism is documented for this constraint.
